decisive_items: Black eschar on the nasal root
Haematoxylin and eosin staining showed presence of large amount of fungal hyphae and spores
Detected 22 sequence reads of Rhizopus microsporum (0.16% of all reads)
response.rationale: The vignette describes classic rhinocerebral mucormycosis in an uncontrolled diabetic: black eschar, fungal hyphae, and Rhizopus/Mucor detection. R1 (Mucormycosis) is the overarching diagnosis, while R4 (Rhizopus infection) is a specific pathogen but less complete. Other candidates misattribute to aspergillosis, COVID-19 alone, or non-specific sinusitis.

rejected.why: Aspergillosis is contradicted by Rhizopus/Mucor detection and black eschar; COVID-19 association is secondary.
Invasive aspergillosis is contradicted by Rhizopus microsporum and Mucor racemosus, not Aspergillus.
Fungal sinusitis is too broad and misses the invasive mucormycosis pattern.
COVID-19 alone does not explain the fungal hyphae, black eschar, or Rhizopus detection.
Diabetic ketoacidosis is not supported; the presentation is fungal infection, not DKA.
Pansinusitis is a finding, not a diagnosis; it lacks the fungal and invasive context.
